site.aboutStory:
We started with one Pomeranian and a lot of questions about how to raise small dogs well. Today we work with a handful of carefully selected breeds and a dedicated vet partner.

Our puppies grow up inside our home, around everyday sounds and people. By the time they leave, they're used to handling, grooming and short car rides.

breeds.name: Pomeranian
breeds.blurb: Fox-like face, big personality, lots of fluff.
breeds.description: Pomeranians are bold, curious and loyal. Their thick double coat and bright expression make them one of the most popular toy breeds. They are alert little watchdogs and love being the centre of attention.

breeds.blurb: Silky white coat and a calm, loving nature.

breeds.name: Toy Poodle
breeds.blurb: Smart, hypoallergenic and easy to train.
breeds.description: Toy Poodles are among the most intelligent dog breeds. They learn quickly, shed very little and come in many colours, from red and apricot to black and white.

breeds.name: Yorkshire Terrier
breeds.blurb: Brave little companion with a silky coat.
breeds.description: Yorkies are confident, energetic and affectionate. Their fine, hair-like coat sheds little, and they carry a big-dog attitude in a tiny body.
breeds.grooming: Brush daily if kept long; or a short puppy cut

breeds.name: Chihuahua
breeds.blurb: Tiny, loyal and full of spirit.
breeds.description: The smallest breed in the world, the Chihuahua forms a deep bond with its owner. Chihuahuas are lively, alert and easy to carry everywhere.

breeds.name: French Bulldog
breeds.description: Frenchies are relaxed, funny and affectionate. They need little exercise and are happy in small homes, but they don't tolerate heat well.

breeds.name: Pomsky
breeds.blurb: Husky looks in a compact, cuddly size.
breeds.description: A cross between a Pomeranian and a Siberian Husky, the Pomsky has striking looks, often with blue eyes. Pomskies are playful and energetic and need daily activity.

breeds.name: Bichon Frise
breeds.description: Bichons are happy, sociable and gentle. Their curly white coat sheds very little, and they get along with children, other dogs and visitors.

posts.title: How to Choose the Right Small Breed for Your Home
posts.excerpt: Energy, shedding, size and temperament: a practical guide to matching a toy breed to the way you live.
posts.body:
Small dogs share a size category, not a personality. A Chihuahua and a Maltipoo can weigh the same and still need very different homes. Before you fall in love with a photo, check how each breed fits these four areas of your life.

1. Your space and schedule

Apartment living suits most toy breeds, but some handle being alone better than others. Maltese and Bichons are happiest with company for most of the day. Yorkies and Chihuahuas are a little more independent once they are adults. If you work long hours away from home, plan for a dog walker or daycare whichever breed you choose.

2. Allergies and shedding

If anyone in the home has allergies, look at low-shedding coats: Toy Poodle, Maltipoo, Maltese and Bichon Frise. No dog is fully hypoallergenic, so spend time around the breed before deciding.

3. Grooming time

A Pomeranian's double coat needs brushing three to four times a week. Poodle-type coats need a professional trim every six to eight weeks. A French Bulldog needs little brushing but regular cleaning of its facial folds. Grooming is a real cost in both time and money, so budget for it.

4. Children and other pets

Very small puppies can be hurt by an accidental drop or a rough game. With young children, a sturdier small breed such as a Maltipoo, Bichon or French Bulldog is often the safer choice.

Quick match guide

  • First-time owner: Maltipoo, Bichon Frise
  • Allergy-friendly: Toy Poodle, Maltese
  • Big personality: Pomeranian, Chihuahua
  • Low exercise: French Bulldog
  • Active family: Pomsky

Still unsure? Message us on WhatsApp and tell us about your home. We will suggest two or three breeds that fit.

posts.title: Bringing Your Puppy Home: The First 7 Days
posts.excerpt: A day-by-day plan for settling in, from the car ride home to the first vet visit.
posts.body:
The first week sets the tone for everything that follows. Keep it calm, keep it simple and stick to a routine.

Before day one

  • A small crate or playpen with a soft bed
  • The same food your puppy is already eating
  • Puppy pads, an enzyme cleaner and a few chew toys
  • A lightweight harness (not a collar) for tiny breeds
  • A nutritional gel in case of low blood sugar

Days 1–2: Quiet arrival

Limit visitors. Show your puppy its bed, water and potty spot, then let it rest. Toy puppies sleep 18–20 hours a day, and that is normal. Some crying at night is also normal; a warm blanket that smells of its litter helps.

Days 3–4: Build the routine

Feed at the same times every day. Take your puppy to the potty spot after every meal, nap and play session. Praise every success, and clean accidents with an enzyme cleaner so the smell doesn't draw the puppy back.

Days 5–6: Gentle socialization

Introduce new sounds, surfaces and calm people in short sessions. Keep your puppy off public ground until its vaccinations are complete, but you can carry it outside to see the world.

Day 7: First vet check

Book a wellness visit within the first week. Bring the vaccination and deworming records from your puppy pack. This visit is also required to keep your health guarantee active.

Watch for these signs

Small breeds can develop low blood sugar. If your puppy seems weak, wobbly or very sleepy and won't eat, rub a little honey or nutritional gel on its gums and call your vet right away.

posts.title: Feeding a Toy Puppy: Schedules That Work
posts.excerpt: How often to feed, how much, and how to prevent the blood-sugar dips small puppies are prone to.
posts.body:
Tiny puppies have tiny stomachs and fast metabolisms. They need small meals often, especially in the first months.

How often

  • 8–12 weeks: 4 meals a day
  • 3–6 months: 3 meals a day
  • 6 months and up: 2 meals a day

What to feed

Choose a small-breed puppy formula with a small kibble size. Keep the food your puppy came home with for at least two weeks, then switch gradually over 7–10 days if you want to change brands. Mix a little more of the new food in each day.

Preventing low blood sugar

Hypoglycemia is the most common emergency in toy breeds. Never skip a meal, keep a high-calorie supplement gel at home, and offer a snack after long play sessions or travel.

Treats and water

Treats should stay under 10% of daily calories. Fresh water should be available at all times. Use a shallow bowl that a small puppy can reach easily.

Foods to avoid

Chocolate, grapes, raisins, onions, garlic, xylitol (found in sugar-free gum), macadamia nuts and cooked bones are all dangerous for dogs.

posts.title: How Puppy Delivery Works: Cargo vs Flight Nanny
posts.excerpt: What each option involves and how to choose the safest way to get your puppy home.
posts.body:
If you can't pick up in person, there are two main ways to bring your puppy home. Both are safe when arranged properly.

Option 1: Pet cargo

Your puppy travels in a climate-controlled, pressurized area of the plane in an airline-approved crate. You collect it at the cargo office at your destination airport.

  • Lower cost
  • Available on most major routes
  • Airlines may restrict travel in very hot or cold months

Option 2: Flight nanny

A trained handler flies in the cabin with your puppy under the seat and hands it to you at arrivals.

  • Your puppy is never out of sight
  • Best for very small or young puppies
  • Higher cost, quoted per route

Paperwork that travels with your puppy

A vet health certificate issued within 10 days of travel, the vaccination record and the microchip number. International trips may also need an import permit and a minimum age, so always check the rules for your country.

Our recommendation

For puppies under 4 lb, we suggest a flight nanny. Message us on WhatsApp with your city and we will send you both quotes.

posts.title: How to Spot a Puppy Scam and Buy Safely
posts.excerpt: Fake listings are common. These checks protect you and your money before you send a deposit.
posts.body:
Puppy scams use stolen photos and pressure tactics. A few simple checks will protect you.

Red flags

  • Prices far below what other breeders charge
  • The seller refuses a live video call
  • Payment only by gift card, crypto or a money transfer app
  • Sudden extra fees for "insurance" or "special crates" after you pay
  • Photos that appear on other websites (try a reverse image search)

What a real breeder will do

  • Show you the puppy live on video, on request
  • Send a written contract and health guarantee before payment
  • Share vet records and the vet clinic's details
  • Give you a registered business name you can look up

Verify you're talking to us

We only message from the WhatsApp number listed on this website. If someone contacts you claiming to be us from another number, don't pay. Message our official number to confirm.

Pay safely

Use a card or a bank transfer to our registered business account, and always ask for a receipt for every payment.

process.title: How to Buy
process.summary: Choose, meet on video, reserve and bring your puppy home.
process.body:
Reserving your puppy

  1. Pick a puppy from the available list, or tell us what you're looking for.
  2. Video call. We show you the puppy live and answer your questions.
  3. Deposit. A deposit reserves your puppy and marks it as reserved on the website.
  4. Agreement. You sign our adoption agreement and receive the health guarantee.
  5. Balance and delivery. Pay the balance before pickup or delivery.

Payment methods

Card, bank transfer or financing. We never ask for gift cards or crypto.

process.title: Health Guarantee
process.summary: One-year written guarantee on genetic and congenital conditions.

One-year health guarantee

Every puppy has a full vet examination before going home. Our written guarantee covers genetic and congenital conditions diagnosed by a licensed vet within 12 months.

What's included

  • Vet health certificate
  • Age-appropriate vaccinations and deworming
  • Microchip
  • Replacement puppy or partial refund if a covered condition is diagnosed

Your part

Take your puppy for a vet check within 7 days of arrival and keep vaccinations up to date.

legal.title: Privacy Policy
legal.body:
We collect the information you give us when you contact us by WhatsApp, email or our contact form: your name, phone number, email address and message. We use it only to answer your questions and to arrange your puppy's reservation and delivery.

We do not sell your personal information. We share it only with service providers needed to complete your order, such as payment processors and delivery partners.

You can ask us to see, correct or delete your information at any time by contacting us.

legal.title: Terms of Service
legal.body:
By using this website you agree to these terms. Puppy listings, prices and availability may change without notice. A puppy is only reserved once a deposit is received and confirmed in writing.

All sales are governed by the adoption agreement signed at the time of reservation.

legal.title: Refund Policy
legal.body:
Deposits are non-refundable but can be moved to another puppy. If your chosen puppy does not pass its final vet check, your deposit is transferred to another puppy of your choice or refunded in full.

Health-related claims are handled under our one-year health guarantee.
